transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (AcornBio SRE), Liam O'Connor (AcornBio Platform), Dr. Sumi Rao (AcornBio CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Walkthrough of Console trace playback, request logs, and fallback policies.
- Focus on reproducing a 95thp latency spike and verifying KV cache behavior.
- Security checklist requested (SOC2 + network diagram).
- Agreement to run an on-prem pilot for sensitive PHI workloads.

Topics covered:
- Trace playback / request inspector
- Error sleuthing and root-cause patterns
- KV cache invalidation and cache cold/warm behavior
- Fallback model policy and routing implications
- Observability instrumentation (tracing headers, sampling)
- Security and compliance questions (SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How are you folks doing?
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: Good, thanks. We have about an hour, so hoping to get into the playback flow and then show you a couple of problem traces that tripped our nightly jobs.
[00:20] Priya Desai: Awesome. Quick agenda, we'll do a quick console walkthrough - trace playback, request logs, then dig into an example error path with fallback and finally talk about security and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:32] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. We also want to understand the KV cache behavior, we think cache eviction is causing rehydration spikes.
[00:40] Priya Desai: Great, we'll cover that. Alright screen share in 3, 2, 1.
[00:48] [screen shares, slight audio rustle] Priya Desai: Okay, so this is the Redwoo Console - sorry, Redwood Console - our Request Inspector. Top left you can filter by model, route, tenant id. I'm going to filter to AcornBio-prod, last 24 hours.
[01:05] Marta Ruiz: Quick note, our traces include a custom header X-Acorn-Trace, so we can find the exact request id.
[01:12] Priya Desai: Perfect, use that filter. Here you can see a list of requests with latency, token counts, and a small sparkline. There's an action to play back the request which replays the exact input through the same model variant and pipeline.
[01:28] [15s silence while attendees scan screen]
[01:43] Priya Desai: I'll open a slow request from last night, 95th percentile spike around 03:12 UTC. Clicking into it shows the request timeline, the KV cache hits and misses, and the per-step latencies.
[01:58] Liam O'Connor: That one shows a KV miss at step 2 and then a long kernel execution. Could that be a cold cache on a sharded quantized model?
[02:08] Priya Desai: Yes, what you're seeing is the prefix cache miss during streaming. The console color codes cache hits in green and misses in amber. You can also see fallback events if the primary variant timed out and we routed to a smaller model.
[02:21] Marta Ruiz: When you say fallback event, is that automatic? We saw a lot of degraded outputs when fallback happened.
[02:27] Jordan Kim: Good question. Fallback is policy-driven. You can set latency SLO thresholds per route; if the primary doesn't respond within X ms, the router can route to a cheaper/compatible variant. We log the reason and the input that triggered it, which you can replay.
[02:42] Dr. Sumi Rao: One of our concerns is output fidelity during fallback. We can't have critical clinical summaries degrade. How do you handle quality checks?
[02:51] Priya Desai: We recommend canarying fallback variants with a small percent and running automatic reranks or quality heuristics. In Console you can attach prompt-evals; if the fallback output fails a quality gate, the system can reroute back or flag for human review.
[03:07] [short laugh]
[03:12] Priya Desai: Okay drilling into the timeline, you can expand kernel timings. Notice here the big jump at the NV kernel selection stage. That often correlates with model sharding or a cache miss causing an entire KV re-materialization.
[03:26] Liam O'Connor: Does Redwood surface GPU utilization per-request? We need to trace noisy neighbors.
[03:31] Priya Desai: We show per-request GPU time and an aggregate trace that ties requests to GPU host ids. For Dedicated customers you can also pull host-level trace logs to see co-tenancy patterns.
[03:44] Marta Ruiz: Could you show how we would pull all requests that hit a specific cache key and then export?
[03:50] Priya Desai: Sure. Use the filter query: cache.key:"user-123:prefix-v2" and then Export > CSV or stream to S3. I'll run it now. [keyboard clicks] Here's the export link, also attached to the ticket I sent earlier.
[04:05] Jordan Kim: Quick aside on storage — exports respect your retention settings and for Private deployments exports can be routed to customer S3 or on-prem object storage.
[04:16] Dr. Sumi Rao: Important for PHI. We need exports to never touch Redwood-managed buckets for that pilot.
[04:22] Jordan Kim: Understood, Private mode or Dedicated with VPC endpoint is the usual approach. We'll include the network diagram in the security pack.
[04:31] [pause]
[04:40] Priya Desai: Back to the slow trace, I'm going to replay the exact request. Playback mode has two options: dry-run which simulates, and full-replay which executes against the selected model variant. We'll do dry-run first to show expected time and token counts.
[04:56] [replay simulation audio overlay]
[05:05] Priya Desai: The dry-run shows an expected 1.8s per token but actual was 3.0s because of the cache miss and an intermediate fallback. Now I'll run a full replay to the smaller model to demonstrate the output differences.
[05:22] Marta Ruiz: Can you annotate where the rerank step is? We have a reranker after generation.
[05:28] Priya Desai: Yep, generation step, then rerank step at 1.2s. The console shows a separate stage for reranker latency. You can also replay only through the rerank stage if you want to test reranks in isolation.
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: Is rerank considered in the fallback routing? Like if rerank is slow it triggers fallback?
[05:46] Priya Desai: Currently routing is stage-aware; you can include rerank in the latency SLO or exclude it depending on criticality.
[05:55] [10s pause, typing]
[06:05] Priya Desai: One more thing — Request tags. We saw you use job_id and dataset tags. Console supports persisted tags and you can create dashboards from them.
[06:16] Marta Ruiz: Nice. On the KV cache: what's the TTL policy and any recommended eviction heuristics for high-concurrency workloads?
[06:23] Priya Desai: We recommend a two-tier TTL: short-lived per-request prefixes and longer-lived persona-level caches. For high concurrency, size-based eviction combined with LRU works well; Redwood Optimize can analyze your token patterns and suggest specific cache sizes and quantization knobs.
[06:39] Dr. Sumi Rao: Can Optimize recommend quantization for our models? We use a custom finetune on top of an open model.
[06:45] Jordan Kim: Yes, Optimize suggests quantization profiles informed by your accuracy budgets and throughput goals; for finetunes we recommend a validation-suite run to guard against regressions.
[06:56] [screen change, demo of Optimize recommendations]
[07:05] Priya Desai: Here is an example Optimize report. It shows expected latency reduction vs quality delta at various quant levels. You can export an evaluation harness too.
[07:16] Liam O'Connor: About tracing instrumentation — our services already propagate Jaeger IDs. How do we map those to Redwood request ids?
[07:23] Priya Desai: You can pass X-Trace-Id and we will associate it, or map via request metadata. For Private, the trace propagation is through your collector and we ingest spans based on a small shim we provide.
[07:37] Marta Ruiz: Is there an SDK to inject KV keys and cache hints?
[07:41] Priya Desai: Yes, our SDK supports cache.hint headers and explicit cache.put/cache.get for advanced users. We'll share code snippets.
[07:50] [crosstalk: agreement sounds]
[08:03] Jordan Kim: I want to pivot to incident scenario: we had an alert at 95thp for increased latency. Walk me through how you'd use Console to triage.
[08:12] Priya Desai: Start with the alert link into Console - it lands you on the aggregate timeline centered on the alert window. Use the Model->Route filter, then open the top offenders. From an offender, open request timeline, check cache.hit pattern, kernel selection, and fallback flags. If kernel selection time high across many requests, likely model host or kernel mismatch.
[08:32] Liam O'Connor: Could that be caused by a miscompiled kernel after a model roll?
[08:36] Priya Desai: Yes, if a new kernel or quantized variant is deployed and the runtime selects an incompatible kernel, you can see degraded perf. We surface kernel mismatch warnings in the model rollout page and can auto-fallback to previous variant.
[08:49] Dr. Sumi Rao: What about audit logs? We need a full chain for compliance.
[08:54] Jordan Kim: We provide immutable audit logs for all admin actions, model rollouts, and role changes. For Private you can push logs to your SIEM.
[09:04] Marta Ruiz: Ok show me the playbook steps to replicate the failure locally.
[09:09] Priya Desai: Step 1: identify request ids from the alert window. Step 2: run trace playback in dry-run to verify timing. Step 3: replay against fallback variant to test fidelity. Step 4: if kernel timing is the issue, roll back variant or pin kernel selection via the model config. We'll paste this playbook in the shared doc.
[09:29] [typing sounds]
[09:37] Marta Ruiz: Are there any gotchas for multi-tenant Dedicated pools? We might run Dedicated for production and keep dev on Hosted.
[09:44] Jordan Kim: Dedicated gives you predictability and isolation; we still have routing fallbacks that can route to other Dedicated nodes within your pool if autoscale triggers. For strict isolation you can configure pool-affinity and no cross-tenant bursting.
[09:58] Liam O'Connor: We have an SSO requirement, SAML + SCIM. How granular is RBAC?
[10:03] Priya Desai: RBAC is role-based with custom roles and route-level permissions. SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported for both Hosted and Private. We'll include the SSO config notes in the security pack.
[10:17] Dr. Sumi Rao: Timeline-wise we want to pilot in January and production by end of Q1, assuming benchmarks look good.
[10:24] Jordan Kim: That aligns with typical on-prem pilots. We'll send a pilot runbook and timeline.
[10:31] [short pause]
[10:40] Priya Desai: Back to console features — error analysis view groups similar failures and surfaces a summary reason such as "tokenization error", "kernel OOM", or "timeout fallback". You can open a grouped error and see the sample request and common stack.
[10:56] Marta Ruiz: Tokenization errors show up in our logs sometimes; are those surfaced with exact input?
[11:01] Priya Desai: Yes, but note PII masking can be enabled — raw input is only available to allowed roles and is audited.
[11:11] Liam O'Connor: Can we run synthetic workloads from Console to reproduce noisy neighbor issues?
[11:16] Priya Desai: We have a Replay Lab for synthetic replays. It runs controlled traffic patterns against a cluster and captures detailed perf counters. It's very handy for load-testing cache warm-up strategies.
[11:29] Marta Ruiz: Great. Can you show a sample Replay Lab run?
[11:33] [screen changes, short wait]
[11:40] Priya Desai: Here's a replay that ramps to 200 rps and monitors KV hit rate. Notice warm-up curve at 2 minutes — cache hit rate climbs from 12% to 78% once hot keys are populated.
[11:53] Dr. Sumi Rao: That's helpful. Any recommended prewarm heuristics?
[11:57] Priya Desai: Prime hot prefixes during deploys, and run a short warm-up ramp as part of your CI/CD for model rollout. Optimize can auto-generate the warm-up script based on recent traffic.
[12:11] [brief laughter]
[12:18] Marta Ruiz: Switching gears, our legal team asked about data retention and deletion. If we request deletion for a particular tenant, how is that handled?
[12:26] Jordan Kim: We support tenant-scoped data purge with cryptographic deletion for keys and a full wipe option for Private. Deletion requests are logged and we provide a certificate of deletion for audit.
[12:39] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated, do we get control-plane logs or just metrics?
[12:44] Priya Desai: You get both; control plane events can be streamed to your logging sink and metrics to your Prometheus stack.
[12:53] Marta Ruiz: Ok, show the playback output diff view so we can see where fallback changed output tokens.
[12:59] Priya Desai: Here, side-by-side diffs with token-level highlights and confidence deltas. The console marks tokens that were hallucinated or truncated. You can export this diff to include in incident reports.
[13:15] Dr. Sumi Rao: Any support for deterministic replay to compare outputs across versions?
[13:20] Priya Desai: We support deterministic mode for compatible models, plus controlled seeds and fixed sampling. For finetuned models, we recommend a dedicated eval harness.
[13:33] [pause, pages turning]
[13:42] Jordan Kim: I want to surface one tricky behavior: when requests stream and a KV miss triggers, latency can spike but streaming partial responses reach the client. This can cause incomplete deltas in downstream consumers. How do you mitigate?
[13:58] Priya Desai: Use backpressure and chunk-based re-assembly. Console highlights partial stream interruptions and you can set a fallback that waits for full generation before sending to end users, at the cost of extra latency.
[14:12] Marta Ruiz: We may accept that if clinical summaries require completeness.
[14:17] Priya Desai: Totally. That can be a route-level policy.
[14:22] [short silence]
[14:32] Liam O'Connor: A couple of implementation questions — do we need a network egress rule to allow playback to reach our on-prem model hosts?
[14:38] Jordan Kim: For Private on-prem, playback runs within your network. For Dedicated with VPC peering, you'll need to open ports for the Redwood agent to reach your hosts if you use on-prem model serving. We'll include a diagram.
[14:50] Dr. Sumi Rao: Encryption at rest specifics? We need HSM-backed KMS.
[14:55] Jordan Kim: Supported; Private and Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We also provide HSM-backed key wrap for private key material.
[15:07] [typing]
[15:18] Priya Desai: Ok switching to a live debug: I'm going to show a grouped error cluster labeled "fallback-induced hallucination". It aggregates 46 similar requests. Opening one shows input, the fallback chain (primary -> small-variant -> rerank), and the final diff.
[15:34] Marta Ruiz: In the group summary, is there a way to bulk re-evaluate with a different reranker?
[15:38] Priya Desai: Yes, bulk re-eval lets you select a set and run them through an alternate reranker or new model version; results stream back to an S3 bucket.
[15:48] Liam O'Connor: That could save a lot of manual repro.
[15:51] Priya Desai: Exactly.
[15:56] [short pause]
[16:05] Priya Desai: Now, on instrumentation: if you want to trace downstream service calls (e.g., a DB lookup) we surface external calls as part of the request timeline. You can add custom span tags to help correlate.
[16:20] Marta Ruiz: Our issue last week had a slow DB call inside a prompt preprocessor. Can we isolate that without replaying the model?
[16:26] Priya Desai: Yes, timeline includes pre and post processing stages. You can replay only the preprocessor locally or in a sandbox. Console flags slow external spans with a link to the log lines.
[16:39] [noise in background, someone coughs]
[16:44] Dr. Sumi Rao: About SLAs for 99thp latency — is that available for Dedicated?
[16:50] Jordan Kim: Yes, Dedicated SLA covers throughput and a latency target for provisioned pools. We'll share the SLA doc. For strict requirements we recommend Dedicated plus reserved instances.
[17:02] Liam O'Connor: Any differences in trace fidelity between Hosted and Private?
[17:06] Priya Desai: Fidelity is the same, but for Private you control retention and collectors. Hosted has a higher default retention but you can opt-in to longer retention paid tiers.
[17:20] Marta Ruiz: Ok, can you show the audit trail for a model rollout that included a kernel change? We want to see who pushed it and which hosts were affected.
[17:28] [screen shows audit timeline] Priya Desai: Here's a rollout event, you can expand to show commit id, who approved, which kernels were selected, and automatic fallback triggers.
[17:41] Jordan Kim: We can also pin a previous kernel via the API. That helps during emergency mitigation.
[17:49] Marta Ruiz: What's the usual turnaround to get support on a P1?
[17:53] Jordan Kim: For Enterprise tier customers we have a 30-minute paging SLA for P1s and a dedicated TAM option. We'll include the support SLAs.
[18:03] [brief pause]
[18:12] Priya Desai: One last demo bit — Request Forensics. You can start with a failing request and the console surfaces candidate root causes with confidence scores and suggested remediations (e.g., increase cache TTL, pin model, or change sampling).
[18:29] Liam O'Connor: How accurate are those suggestions? Are they heuristics?
[18:33] Priya Desai: Mostly heuristic with a rules engine informed by signal patterns. We always recommend validating changes in Replay Lab first.
[18:43] Marta Ruiz: Could you attach the rule set? Our ops team wants to vet them.
[18:48] Jordan Kim: We'll include the rule doc and the exact logic used to flag causes.
[18:55] [longer pause while attendees review docs]
[19:25] Dr. Sumi Rao: Quick question on cost — routing to fallback increases token cost sometimes because of double generation. How do you estimate cost impact?
[19:33] Jordan Kim: Console provides per-request cost breakdown: primary generation cost, fallback cost, rerank cost, and total. Optimize can run simulation to estimate monthly spend under different fallback policies.
[19:46] Liam O'Connor: Could we throttle fallback to limit budget impact?
[19:50] Priya Desai: Yes, you can cap fallback percent or set budget-based policies that only allow fallback if budget threshold not exceeded.
[19:59] [typing]
[20:12] Marta Ruiz: Our security team will want the network diagram and SOC2. Also a sample Data Processing Agreement.
[20:19] Jordan Kim: Noted. We'll send SOC2 + DPA + network diagram as next steps.
[20:26] Priya Desai: Also attaching the replay runbook, the Optimize recommendation sample, and a short code snippet for SDK cache hints.
[20:36] [crosstalk: thanks]
[20:45] Dr. Sumi Rao: About the on-prem pilot — what infra do we need? GPUs? Specific drivers?
[20:51] Priya Desai: For on-prem we provide a lightweight agent and recommend Nvidia A100 or H100 depending on your throughput. We'll include driver versions and kernel deps in the pilot doc.
[21:05] Liam O'Connor: If we want determinism we'll need to pin cuDNN versions too?
[21:09] Priya Desai: Correct, pinning cuDNN, CUDA, and the runtime is recommended for deterministic behavior. We'll provide a reproducibility checklist.
[21:22] Marta Ruiz: Is there any partial automation for failover tests? We want to run weekly failover drills.
[21:28] Priya Desai: Yes, we can schedule synthetic failover tests via the Console and run a canary and failover exercise; results are captured in a report.
[21:40] [pause]
[21:49] Jordan Kim: Let's capture explicit next steps so no one leaves with ambiguity.
[21:54] Jordan Kim: Priya, can you list what you'll deliver?
[21:58] Priya Desai: Sure: (1) Security pack with SOC2 + network diagram + DPA template, (2) Benchmark runbook and sample replay results for the slow trace, (3) Optimize recommendation export, (4) SDK snippets for cache hints. I'll target Dec 17 for the security pack and Dec 20 for the bench artifacts.
[22:18] Jordan Kim: Marta/Liam, can you confirm what you'll share?
[22:23] Marta Ruiz: We'll export the sample request ids, traces, and a minimal dataset for the pilot by Dec 18. Also the legal contacts for DPA.
[22:33] Liam O'Connor: We'll review the replay results and schedule the on-prem pilot kickoff for Jan 6.
[22:39] Dr. Sumi Rao: Sounds good.
[22:41] [longer silence while people take notes]
[23:05] Priya Desai: One small note on noisy neighbors: if you see periodic latency spikes tied to autoscale, consider configuring burst capacity thresholds and a warm-up policy. That usually addresses rehydration storms.
[23:20] Marta Ruiz: Ok. Also, can Redwood support a custom rule to block fallback for certain route tags like clinical-summary?
[23:27] Priya Desai: Absolutely, route-level deny-fallback tags are supported. We'll show the policy config in the sample.
[23:38] [discussion about policy syntax]
[23:50] Jordan Kim: Alright, I think we're approaching time. Any other open questions?
[23:55] Marta Ruiz: One last quick one — can we export the token-level cost for a month to compare costs across rollouts?
[24:02] Jordan Kim: Yes, cost export is route and token-level, and we can correlate with model variants and dates. We'll attach a sample CSV.
[24:12] Dr. Sumi Rao: Great. Thanks everyone, very helpful demo.
[24:16] Jordan Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts. I'll capture the action items.
[24:22] [meeting closes; remaining 38 minutes were Q/A and detailed replay run which is summarized below due to recording policy]

Summarized extended Q/A (recording omitted clips)
- 24:22-35:00: Priya ran two full replays in Replay Lab (200 rps synthetic warm-up, then a focused reproduce of the 95thp trace). Observations: KV miss correlated with host migration; suggested pinning host kernels for the rollout window.
- 35:00-44:00: Jordan and Priya walked through Optimize recommendations; showed quantization tradeoffs for finetuned model and produced an eval harness (accuracy drop ~0.7% at 4-bit but 2.6x throughput improvement).
- 44:00-52:30: Security/Compliance deep-dive with Jordan and the Acorn legal/infosec leads. Confirmed SAML+SCIM, KMS integrations, audit log streaming options.
- 52:30-60:00: Logistics and pilot planning; agreed on Jan 6 kickoff and identified internal stakeholders.
